The simplest way to think about it: Qi2 is the magnetic 15W standard, Qi2.2 is the faster 25W version, and MagSafe is Apple's magnetic charging technology and accessory ecosystem. The important catch is that your phone and charger both need to support the faster charging rate.

Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe
1. Qi2
Up to 15W

An open wireless-charging standard developed by the Wireless Power Consortium, incorporating magnetic alignment technology inspired by Apple's MagSafe.

Magnets snap your phone into the correct charging position.

Works with compatible iPhones and select Android phones.

Typically offers up to 15W wireless charging.

Source: Wireless Power Consortium

2. Qi2.2 / Qi2 25W
Up to 25W

The faster generation of Qi2, officially branded Qi2 25W for the Qi v2.2.1 standard.

Raises maximum wireless charging power from 15W to 25W.

Retains magnetic alignment and interoperability.

Can charge compatible phones from 0% to around 50% in roughly 30 minutes under suitable conditions.

Best for: people who want faster wireless charging without being limited to Apple's own charger brand.

Source: Wireless Power Consortium

3. MagSafe
Apple ecosystem

Apple's proprietary magnetic attachment and charging technology for compatible iPhones and accessories.

Snaps into place magnetically.

Supports charging at up to 25W with compatible newer iPhones and the appropriate charger and power adapter.

The latest Apple MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W and Qi, so it supports more than just MagSafe charging.

Best for: iPhone owners who want Apple's own charger and straightforward compatibility.

Source: Apple MagSafe Charger

One important compatibility warning

A 25W charger doesn't automatically mean your phone will charge at 25W. Your phone's supported standard, model, power adapter, temperature and charging conditions all matter. Some Android phones are marketed as “Qi2 Ready,” which means they need a compatible magnetic case to get the magnetic alignment benefits.

For example, Apple's supplied specifications say the latest MagSafe Charger can deliver up to 25W with compatible newer iPhones and a suitable 30W adapter, while other models charge more slowly. Apple's specifications

My recommendation: If you're buying for a newer iPhone, choose a certified Qi2 25W or MagSafe charger. If you're buying for Android, verify your exact phone model's Qi2 support before paying extra for 25W.
